A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Eyes Wide Unshut research by the same authors. All eight pages of v1 and ten pages of v3 were readable, including equations, figures, tables, and references. Neither supplied PDF contains a separate appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original EPIC-Tent mistake-detection experiments, gaze-estimation results, and qualitative predictions in Tables I–II and Figure 4.

after.justification: v3 reports original experiments on EPIC-Tent, HoloAssist, and IndustReal, plus fusion ablations, an uncertainty–mistake regression, and failure analyses.

M1.justification: v3 adds correlation fusion using an input trajectory token, transformer attention, and a dedicated gaze-visual correlation module. Its main configuration combines channel and correlation fusion, replacing v1's ensemble averaging early- and mid-fusion predictions. The earlier fusion mechanisms remain as channel and sum fusion; those renamings are not new components.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates only EPIC-Tent tent assembly. v3 additionally evaluates industrial procedural activities in IndustReal and varied expert-assisted tasks in HoloAssist (Section 4.1, Tables 4–5). These datasets were merely cited in v1; their actual evaluation substantially broadens represented activities and environments.

E2.justification: Random, TrajREC, MoCoDAD, and GLC remain the main comparators; v1's Gaze Prediction baseline is GLC. However, the one-class GLC comparisons using entropy, Euclidean distance, and DTW in v1 Table I disappear. The gaze-estimation comparison also replaces the mid/sum-fusion variant with channel-plus-correlation fusion (Table II versus Table 2).

E3.justification: v3 introduces specified training/validation/test partitions for IndustReal and training/test partitions for HoloAssist. It revises EPIC-Tent's reported mistake-frame total from 151,821 to 151,689, without establishing that earlier experiments were rerun. The EPIC-Tent split ratio, evaluation metrics, stride, clip length, and batch size remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 expands the existing fusion analysis to correlation fusion and all combinations of three fusion strategies, although it drops the earlier one-class scoring/fusion breakdown. It also adds an uncertainty–mistake logistic regression, action-class failure distributions, and an illustrative comparison of attention patterns (Section 4.4; Figures 1, 4–5). The earlier qualitative examples are retained as Figure 6.

E5.justification: v3 adds statistical inference through a logistic-regression coefficient of 0.68 with p < 0.001 (Section 4.4); v1 reports no corresponding statistical test. Neither version discloses repeated-run counts, seeds, or confidence intervals for benchmark performance. The new uncertainty boxplot describes self-reported uncertainty, not variability across model runs.

E6.justification: The new channel-plus-correlation model reports unsupervised EPIC-Tent AUC/F1 of 0.69/0.51, versus 0.64/0.49 for v1's different early/mid ensemble. Newly reported unsupervised AUCs are 0.59 on HoloAssist and 0.62 on IndustReal. Gaze-estimation and analysis results are added or replaced, and retained entries also change, including Random F1 from 0.35 to 0.36 and mid/sum-fusion recall from 0.77 to 0.82. These are revised results, not a controlled same-model performance gain.

T1.justification: The Euclidean and heatmap score definitions change their summation ranges from i = 0 through F to i = F/2 + 1 through F, aligning scoring with the unobserved half-trajectory (v1 Equations 2 and 5; v3 Equations 1 and 4). This is a limited mathematical specification correction. Neither version provides theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The central claim of detecting mistakes through unpredictable gaze remains. However, v3 adds the Gaze-Frame Correlation module as an explicit novel contribution, expands the claimed benchmark contribution to three datasets, and adds a first-place HoloAssist Mistake Detection challenge claim in the abstract and conclusion.

C2.justification: v1 says better gaze prediction is not necessarily required for better mistake detection; v3 instead interprets its selected comparisons as suggesting good gaze prediction is essential. v3 also explains possible redundancy and optimization difficulties in sum fusion, interprets the uncertainty association and action-specific failures, and explicitly identifies key-step ordering errors as a limitation.

D1.justification: v3 newly specifies non-overlapping eight-frame windows, gives EPIC-Tent mistake counts by split, identifies Euclidean distance within DTW, and points to FastDTW. It also promises public code and model checkpoints, without establishing their availability. The window description is additional disclosure; v1 does not establish a different overlapping-window procedure.

R1.justification: The four related-work areas and reliance on GLC remain. v3 adds citations to Segment Anything, Salvador and Chan's DTW work, and Seminara et al.'s differentiable task-graph work, while removing the head-mounted IMU attention citation. It also explicitly positions correlation fusion as inspired by GLC's global-local fusion.

P1.justification: The abstract and contribution statements are substantially rewritten, the introduction gains a worked motivation example, and existing related-work summaries are condensed. The method explanation is reorganized around input/output processing and fusion mechanisms, while the experimental narrative separates ablations from competitor comparisons. Terminology, section hierarchy, and the title also change.

P2.justification: The overview and architecture diagrams are substantially redrawn, and the scoring illustration gains an entropy panel. The former broad comparison table is reorganized into ablation and competitor tables, alongside new dataset tables and uncertainty/failure plots. The document adopts a different layout and typography. The existing qualitative panel moves from Figure 4 to Figure 6.

improvement.justification: v1's broad applicability argument rested on one tent-assembly dataset. v3 substantially strengthens validation through two different activity settings and ablations isolating correlation fusion, while adding evidence about uncertainty and explicit limitations concerning ordering errors. The stronger assertion that good gaze prediction is essential exceeds what the comparisons establish, particularly after omitting v1's mid-fusion counterexample. Nevertheless, the broader empirical support and clearer applicability boundaries outweigh that interpretive weakness.
